title: Pula Prices and Realistic Budget for 2027
metaDescription: What Pula costs in 2027: daily budgets, hotel and apartment rates, meals, Arena ticket, buses and beach costs, plus ways to save in Istria's largest city.
content:
## How Much Does Pula Cost in 2027?

Pula sits in the middle of Croatian coastal pricing: cheaper than Dubrovnik, Hvar or Split in peak summer, but no longer a bargain. Daily budgets per person, excluding flights, run roughly like this:

- **Budget:** €50–80 (hostel or small apartment, self-catering, public transport, free sights)
- **Mid-range:** €120–200 (3-star hotel or apartment, restaurant meals twice a day, one or two paid activities)
- **Luxury:** €300 and up (4–5★ hotel, fine dining, boat trips)

A couple travelling mid-range should plan for €240–400 per day in July and August. Outside summer, the same trip often falls to €180–300.

## How Have Prices in Pula Changed Recently?

Prices have risen steadily since Croatia adopted the euro on 1 January 2023. Restaurants, coffee and accommodation all moved up, and the conversion period made many menus round upward. Accommodation shows the biggest change. A three-star hotel now typically costs €110–180 per night in peak season, where many travellers once found rooms near €70–90.

The Arena is a counter-example. Adult admission stays at €10, with €5 for children, pupils and students, and free entry for children under five. Treat that as one of the few sights where price pressure has been modest.

For 2027, expect increases of about 3–6% on food and lodging rather than a jump. Summer weeks and event dates carry the largest swings, so a rate that looks high in July can be 30–40% lower in late September.

## Accommodation Costs

### Hotels

Mid-range hotels (3–4★) cost about €100–160 per night for two adults, with peak July–August rates reaching €180. Four- and five-star resorts start around €250. Rooms near the Arena and Forum cost the most. Hotels around Verudela and Stoja are usually cheaper out of season but quieter in the evening.

### Apartments and hostels

Private apartments often start around €50–75 per night off-peak and climb steeply in summer. Hostel beds cost €15–25 per night. Camp Stoja, a campsite on the Stoja peninsula, suits budget travellers who want sea access. It is a 20-minute walk or short bus ride from the Old Town.

### Where to stay

The Old Town is the obvious base for a first visit: the Arena, Forum, Temple of Augustus and most restaurants are within a 10-minute walk. The Verudela and Stoja peninsulas, south of the centre, have pine-backed rocky coves and concrete swimming platforms. They suit beach-first stays.

## Food and Drink Prices

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Espresso | about €1.40–1.80 |
| Burek | €2–3 |
| Pizza or pasta lunch | €8–12 |
| Casual local meal | €10–18 |
| Konoba dinner with a drink | €25–40 |
| Beer (Tomislav, Karlovačko) | €3–4 |
| Three-course dinner for two with wine | €70–120 |
| Fine dining, no drinks | €40–70+ |

Truffle pasta is the Istrian signature and usually costs €15–22 in a konoba. Fresh fish is the real budget-breaker: €18–30 per person for a fish plate, more if it is sold by weight. Batelina, a well-known seafood restaurant in Banjole just outside Pula, and Valsabbion, an upscale restaurant in the Pješčana Uvala area, are the best-known names for seafood and fine dining.

A tight food budget works at €25–35 per day using bakeries, markets and one cooked meal. The covered Pula market near the Forum is the cheapest place for cheese, cured meat, fruit and bread.

## Attractions, Transport and Extras

- **Pula Arena:** €10 adults. Allow 45–90 minutes. The last admission is one hour before closing. Walking around the outside is free.
- **Archaeological Museum:** about €4.
- **Brijuni islands tour:** about €35–40.
- **Cape Kamenjak park entry:** about €6–9 per vehicle or person depending on season.
- **Beach loungers:** about €10 per set at organised beaches.
- **Kayak or SUP sunset tour:** from about €50.
- **City bus:** €1.50–2 per ride. A day with several rides adds €3–6.
- **Arena concerts:** tickets ran about €70–200 for 2026 headliners. Expect similar ranges in 2027.

## Sample 2027 Budgets for Pula

### Three days, per person, mid-range
Shoulder season (May, June, September): about €360–480. July–August: €450–600. This covers a hotel or apartment share, two restaurant meals daily, the Arena and a boat or park excursion.

### One week, per person, budget
About €350–550 including a hostel or modest apartment and mostly casual food.

### One week, couple, mid-range
About €1,700–2,800 depending on season, including accommodation.

## Best Time to Visit for Lower Prices

Hotel rates in Pula run lowest from November to April and stay moderate in May, early June, late September and October. July and August are the most expensive months by a clear margin. Late May and mid-September offer swimmable water and open restaurants at noticeably lower room rates. Winter is cheap but some beach restaurants and seasonal services close.

## Money-Saving Tips

- Book summer lodging by February or March. Central apartments sell out first.
- Eat the lunch menu. Many konobas serve a fixed-price lunch that costs a third less than the same dishes at dinner.
- Skip Old Town restaurants directly facing the Arena and Forum for dinner; walk five minutes into side streets for lower prices.
- Swim at Stoja or Verudela instead of paying for a lounger. Rocky platforms are free.
- Buy a bus ticket from the driver only when needed; the centre is compact enough to cover on foot.
- Pula's concerts push hotel prices up sharply on show dates. Check the Arena calendar before fixing travel dates.

## Opinion: Where Visitors Overspend

Paying for an organised Arena-plus-Old-Town tour on top of the ticket rarely makes sense. The centre is flat, compact and signposted, and the €10 ticket plus an hour of wandering covers 90% of the value. Put that money into a fish dinner or a Brijuni boat trip instead.

## Practical Notes

- Currency: euro. Cards are accepted almost everywhere, but small cafés and market stalls may prefer cash.
- Tipping: optional; rounding up or adding 5–10% in restaurants is normal.
- Arena opening hours change by season, with the longest days in summer. Check the official site for the current schedule before travelling.
- Pula Airport is about 6 km from the centre. Taxis cost roughly €20–30 to the Old Town; some visitors use pre-booked transfers.

faq.question: How much money do I need per day in Pula in 2027?
faq.answer: Budget travellers need about €50–80 per day, mid-range travellers €120–200, and luxury travellers €300 or more. Per-person costs drop if two people share an apartment or hotel room.

faq.question: Is Pula expensive compared with other Croatian cities?
faq.answer: Pula is moderately priced. It costs less than Dubrovnik, Split or Hvar in summer, but more than inland Croatia. Peak July and August prices are the main reason it feels expensive.

faq.question: How much does the Pula Arena cost?
faq.answer: Adult admission is €10, and children, pupils and students pay €5. Children under five enter free, and walking around the outside is free.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Pula?
faq.answer: A casual meal costs €10–18 per person. A konoba dinner with a drink is typically €25–40, and fine dining with truffle menus starts around €40–70 without drinks.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Pula?
faq.answer: November to April has the lowest prices, but some seasonal venues close. May, June, September and October offer a good balance of lower rates, warm weather and open restaurants.

faq.question: How much is public transport in Pula?
faq.answer: A single city bus ride costs about €1.50–2. Most Old Town sights are within walking distance, so many visitors spend only €3–6 per day on buses.

faq.question: Will Pula prices rise in 2027?
faq.answer: Expect modest increases of roughly 3–6% on accommodation and dining compared with 2026. Summer weekends and concert dates will see the largest jumps.

quickAnswer: Plan on €50–80 per day on a budget, €120–200 mid-range and €300+ for luxury in Pula in 2027. Peak July–August rates run well above shoulder season. Arena entry is €10, a konoba dinner is €18–30 and a city bus ride is about €2. Expect modest increases on 2026 prices.
